To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CSFs of BI system implementation are influenced by the organizational factors, which include organizational readiness, management commitment, organizational culture, top management support, and organizational structure.
the organizational factors play the key role in the success of a business intelligence system.
the success of implementing a BI system is determined by the organizational factors that include top management support, organizational culture and change management.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the understanding of CSFs for BI system implementation.
understanding and improving BI implementation success in organizations.
understanding the factors that influence BI system implementation and how these factors can be leveraged to ensure successful implementation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BI stakeholders should prioritize the organizational dimension of CSFs ahead of the technical, managerial, and environmental dimensions.
the success of a business intelligence system implementation is contingent upon the organizational factors.
the success or failure of a BI implementation is determined by the interplay of all the CSFs and their associated contextual issues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BI stakeholders should consider the organizational factors as the topmost priority in BI system implementations.
BI stakeholders should focus on the CSFs that are more relevant to their context.
BI stakeholders should pay special attention to the organizational factors in BI system implementation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CSFs for BI systems are not static, rather they are dynamic, contextual, and inter-related.
CSFs for BI system implementation are context dependent and hence, BI stakeholders should consider the context in which they are operating.
BI stakeholders should focus on the organizational dimension as a precursor to the other dimensions.
